title: Apps
subtitle: Deploy a Docker image or a Git repo to a server.
volBackupsDesc: Back up this app's named volumes to a destination, on a schedule or on demand. A file-level copy of the running volume, not a point-in-time snapshot.
volBackupsWarn: Files are archived while the app keeps running, so the copy is not a point-in-time snapshot and may be inconsistent. Don't rely on it for a running database — use the database's own backup (Databases → Backups), or stop the app before backing up.
volRestoreStarted: Restore started — the volume is being overwritten…
volBackupFailed: Volume backup failed — open the run details for the reason
volRestoreConfirm: Restore this backup? It overwrites the current contents of this volume. If it holds a database captured while running, the restored data may be inconsistent or need recovery on first start. File contents, modes, owners and timestamps are restored; symlink ownership and directory timestamps are not.
volExportHint: Generate a temporary download link for this S3 backup to import it on another server.
volExportExpiry: Link expires in 24 hours — paste it into "Import from URL" on the target server.
volImportDesc: Pull a volume's data from a staged tar(.gz) you exported elsewhere (e.g. from an old server) — a migration data-pull.
volImportWarn: This overwrites the target volume — its current contents are wiped before the import.
volImportConfirm: Import into this volume? Its current contents will be wiped and replaced.
dangerDeleteDesc: Permanently remove this application, its container and (optionally) its volumes. This cannot be undone.
analyticsNoDomain: This app has no domain, so there are no visitor requests to analyse. Analytics reads the proxy's access log for the app's own domains, aliases and per-service domains.
analyticsNoData: No visitor requests recorded for this app yet. Data appears shortly after requests reach its domains.
analyticsServerOff: Traffic Analytics is off on {name}, so nothing is being recorded for this app. Turn it on to start counting visitor requests to its domains.
analyticsServerOffReadOnly: Traffic Analytics is off on this app's server. An owner or admin of the server can turn it on.
analyticsClusterNote: This app runs in a cluster. Analytics shows only the requests recorded on its own server, not the other nodes.

files.title: Files
files.desc: Browse and manage this app's persistent volumes.
files.noVolumes: This app doesn't declare any persistent volumes.
files.truncated: Showing the first {count} entries — this folder has more.
files.uploadHint: Choose files to upload to this folder, or drop them here.
files.nameInvalid: Use a name without slashes or control characters (not "." or ".."), at most 255 bytes.
files.modeHint: 3 or 4 octal digits up to 0777. Setuid, setgid and sticky bits can't be set here, and the change is not recursive.
files.deleteFile: Delete {name}? This can't be undone, and no snapshot is taken first.
files.deleteDir: Delete the folder {name} and everything inside it (recursive)? This can't be undone, and no snapshot is taken first.
files.deleteNotEmpty: The folder isn't empty. Delete it and everything inside it?
files.overwriteBody: {name} already exists in this folder. Overwrite it?
files.containerEphemeral: This is the live container filesystem. Changes are lost when the container is recreated, redeployed or restarted from its image. Reading, uploading and creating folders act as the container's root user and ignore file permissions.
files.containerTruncated: This directory is too large to list completely. Type a path in the path field to go straight to what you need.
files.containerNoBinary: Rename, permissions and delete need mv, chmod and rm inside the image.
files.binaryNoEdit: This looks like a binary file, so it can't be edited here. Download it instead.
files.tooBigNoEdit: This file is too large to edit here. Download it instead.
files.encodingNoEdit: This file isn't valid UTF-8 text, so it can't be edited here. Download it instead.
files.lineEndingsNoEdit: This file mixes line-ending styles, so editing it here could change them. Download it instead.
files.changedOnDisk: This file changed since you opened it.
files.queueRetrying: Too many changes at once. Retrying in {seconds}s…
files.datastoreWarn: This app looks like a database or broker and is running. Changing its data files can corrupt it.
files.capOff: File access isn't enabled for this server.
files.writeCapOff: Read-only: file changes aren't enabled for this server.
files.writeCapHint: Grant the "File changes" capability on the server to upload, edit, rename and delete.
files.terminalCapOff: The container filesystem needs the Terminal and Files capabilities on this server.
files.terminalPermOff: The container filesystem needs the terminal permission for this team.
files.agentOld: This server's agent is too old for file changes. Update the agent first.
files.deployInProgress: A deploy is running. File changes are paused until it finishes.
files.clustered: The container filesystem isn't available for clustered apps.
files.notDeployed: The container filesystem is available after the first deploy.

err.not_found: That file or folder no longer exists.
err.exists: Something with that name already exists.
err.not_dir: A part of that path isn't a folder.
err.not_regular: That isn't a regular file (it may be a link or a device).
err.denied: Permission denied. The server refused that change.
err.too_large: That is larger than the allowed size.
err.changed: It changed since you opened it. Reload or overwrite.
err.integrity: The upload didn't verify. Try again.
err.not_configured: File operations aren't configured on this server's agent.
err.busy: The server is busy. Try again in a moment.
err.expired: The request took too long and expired. Try again.
err.no_binary: The container image doesn't include the tool needed for that.
err.failed: The operation failed on the server.
err.rate_limited: Too many changes in a short time. Wait a moment.
err.capability_not_granted: This server hasn't been granted the capability this needs.
err.agent_too_old: This server's agent is too old for that. Update the agent.
err.datastore_running: This app looks like a running database or broker.
err.deploy_in_progress: A deploy is running. Try again when it finishes.
err.unsupported_clustered: The container filesystem isn't available for clustered apps.
err.not_deployed: The app hasn't been deployed yet.

noMetrics: No metrics yet — they appear a few seconds after the container starts.

crash.title: Crash timeline
crash.desc: Why this app's containers died: exit code, OOM kills and the log lines frozen at crash time.
crash.logRedacted: Log tail hidden — you need secret-read access to view it.

deleteConfirm: Delete this app and its container/volumes? This cannot be undone.
deleteConfirmCompose: Delete this compose app? Its containers AND its named volumes (all data) are removed. This cannot be undone — back up volumes first.
keepVolumes: Keep volumes (don't delete this app's data)
removeImages: Also remove this app's built/pulled images (reclaim disk)
pruneNetworks: Also remove its custom networks ({names}) if no other app uses them
pruneBuildCache: Also prune dangling Docker build cache on the build server (shared by every app there, so another build may run slower once)
overviewHint: Use Deploy to build and start this app. The sections on the left hold environment variables, limits, volumes and more.
readOnlyHint: You have read-only access to this app.
iconHint: A square icon shown across the dashboard. Upload a PNG, JPG or WebP — it is cropped to a square PNG (up to 128px) and stored on your own instance.
iconTooLarge: That image is too detailed to store as an icon. Try a simpler one.
noLogs: No logs yet — deploy this app to see build output here.
name: Name
healthTimingsHint: Seconds; leave blank for the default. Raise start period and retries for a slow-booting app so it isn't rolled back prematurely.
extraPortsDesc: Publish additional host ports (TCP/UDP) beyond the app's main port — e.g. metrics, gRPC or a UDP service. Applies on the next deploy.
networkingDesc: How other containers on this server reach this app, a stable name for it, and any extra Docker networks it joins. Applies on the next deploy.
networkingLockedNote: Networking is managed by the --network flag in Docker options; remove it to use these settings.
internalAddressUnmanaged: This app manages its own networking through custom Docker options (--network), so Tugra can't tell how it is reachable.
containerAliasHint: A DNS name (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens) that always points at this app on every network it joins, unique on the server. Names starting with tugra- are reserved.
containerAliasRollingNote: Setting a stable name makes zero-downtime deploys fall back to recreate (a brief downtime), because two copies would answer to the same name during a rolling swap.
extraNetworksDesc: Docker networks this app also joins, one per line. Apps on the same network reach each other by name.
extraNetworksHint: A network that doesn't exist yet is created on deploy. tugra-apps is the shared per-server network that apps without a domain run on.
networksReserved: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Docker built-ins (bridge, host, none) and other tugra-* names are reserved.
networkingRedeploy: Saved — redeploy to apply the new networking.
stopGracePeriodHint: How long Docker waits after the stop signal before killing the container, for a graceful shutdown (1–3600; blank = Docker's default of 10). Applies to deploy swaps, Stop and Restart.
drainSecondsHint: Zero-downtime (rolling) deploys on an app with a domain only: after the new version is healthy, both versions keep serving for this many seconds before the old one is stopped, so in-flight requests can finish (0–300; blank = off).
restartMaxRetriesHint: Stop restarting after this many failed starts (1–1000). Blank = keep retrying.
networkAliasesDesc: Extra DNS names other apps on the same network can reach this app by (docker --network-alias). One per line. Applies on the next deploy.
networkAliasesHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Applies to every network the app joins: its domain network, a linked database, the shared app network and any extra networks.
extraPortsEmpty: No extra ports. The app still serves its main port.
extraPortIncomplete: Enter both the host and container port, or clear the row.
extraPortDup: Host port {port} is already mapped for {protocol}.
extraPortRemoveConfirm: This port stops being published on the next deploy.
basicAuthDesc: Protect this app with a username and password (HTTP Basic Auth). Passwords are hashed and never shown again. Applies on the next deploy.
basicAuthReplaceNote: Saving replaces all users (re-enter every password). Save with no users to remove basic auth.
basicAuthIncomplete: Enter both a username and a password on each row — incomplete rows are not saved.
basicAuthRemoveConfirm: Remove basic auth for everyone? The app becomes publicly reachable until you add users again.
redirectsDesc: Rewrite incoming requests with regular-expression redirects (e.g. move an old path, or force a canonical host). Each rule becomes a Traefik redirect; the first matching rule wins. Applies on the next deploy.
redirectsHint: Use ${1}, ${2}… to reuse captured groups. Leave Permanent off for a temporary (302) redirect. Saving replaces all rules; save with none to remove them.
previewExcludeEnvHint: One env var name per line. These are dropped from a PR preview's env so production secrets never reach an ephemeral preview.
previewLimitHint: Max concurrent previews (blank = unlimited); a new PR beyond the cap evicts the oldest.
autoDeployHint: When on, a push to the tracked branch deploys automatically. Turn off to pause without removing the webhook.
ipAllowlistDesc: One IP or CIDR per line. When set, only these source ranges may reach the app (checked before any auth). Empty allows all. Applies on the next deploy.
pathPrefixDesc: Serve this app under a URL path, e.g. /api (must start with /). Empty serves at the domain root. Applies on the next deploy.
rateLimitDesc: Limit requests per client IP (average per period, with a burst allowance). Behind a CDN or tunnel all clients share one IP. Applies on the next deploy.
watchPathsDesc: One glob per line (leading ! to exclude). When set, a push only deploys if a changed file matches — so a monorepo doesn't rebuild every app on every push. Empty deploys on every push. Applies to the next push.
composePathHint: Path to the compose file inside the repo (default docker-compose.yml). Cloned, validated and run on deploy.
composeHint: Validated on save; changes apply on the next deploy.

cfgMounts.title: Config files
cfgMounts.hint: Files Tugra mounts read-only into your containers. Only the content can be changed. Avoid pasting secrets — config files are stored unencrypted. Changes apply on the next deploy.
cfgMounts.redeploy: Saved — redeploy to apply the new content.

nixpacksCmdHint: Override Nixpacks' auto-detected install / build / start commands. Leave blank to auto-detect. Applies on the next deploy.
containerPortHint: The port your app listens on inside the container (default 80). Set it to e.g. 3000 or 8080 so the proxy routes to the right port.
containerPortCardDesc: The port your app listens on inside the container. The proxy, the published port mapping and the default health check all route to it. Applied on the next deploy.
containerPortInvalid: Enter a whole number between 1 and 65535.
containerPortRedeploy: Saved — redeploy to apply the new port.
empty: Deploy your first app from a Git repo, image, or compose file.
notDeployedBody: Review this app's environment, ports, volumes and domain, then deploy when you're ready.
stopConfirm: Stop this app? It goes offline until you start it again.
descriptionHint: A free-text note for your team. Shown only here; it does not affect the deployment.
descriptionPlaceholder: What this app is for, who owns it, links...
cloneHint: Creates a copy with the same build and settings, placed in the environment you choose (the same one by default). The domain, TLS certificate and webhook are not carried over, volumes start empty, scheduled tasks are copied disabled, and the clone isn't deployed — you deploy it when ready. Cloning to another server also resets the cluster placement.
cloneWarn_cloned_to_server: The clone is on a different server.
cloneWarn_cluster_config_reset: Cluster placement was reset for the new server.
cloneWarn_host_mounts_copied: Host bind mounts were copied; check the paths exist on the target server.
cloneWarn_domain_reset: The custom domain was not copied.
cloneWarn_custom_cert_dropped: The custom TLS certificate was not copied.
cloneWarn_host_port_reset: The published host port was reset.
cloneWarn_port_mappings_copied: Compose port mappings were copied; review them for conflicts.
cloneWarn_cpuset_reset: CPU pinning was cleared because the target server has fewer cores.
cloneWarn_privileged_options_dropped: Privileged Docker options were not copied; the clone starts non-privileged and an owner can re-enable them.
cloneWarn_other: Some settings were not copied; review the clone before deploying.
restartHint: Restart the running container (same image, no rebuild)
quickRollbackNone: No earlier version to roll back to
redeployHint: Rebuild from the latest source and replace the running container
noBuildOutput: No build output — image pulled and started.
deployHooksDesc: Run a command in a container of this app's image before the swap (e.g. database migrations) and inside the live container after the health check passes. A failing pre-deploy command aborts the deploy with the current version still serving; a post-deploy command is best-effort. Single-server apps only; applies on the next deploy.
deployHooksRedeploy: Saved. Hooks run on the next deployment.
webhookDesc: Add this URL + secret to your repository's webhooks (GitHub, GitLab, Gitea/Forgejo or Bitbucket). A push to {branch} redeploys automatically; with previews enabled, pull/merge request events create and remove previews.
regenerateConfirm: Regenerate the webhook secret? The old one stops working.
envDesc: Stored encrypted. Injected at deploy through a private env file, never as docker arguments. Multiline values are passed by name through the Docker CLI's environment instead.
envDescSwarm: Stored as a Docker secret and decrypted only inside the running container — never written to the cluster's shared config store (needs an image with a shell; distroless images fall back to standard env).
envRedeploy: Saved — redeploy to apply the new values.
envDupWarning: Duplicate keys: {keys}. Rename or remove — only one value per key can be saved.
envInvalidWarning: Not valid env var names: {keys}. Use letters, digits and underscores (must not start with a digit).
envRowDup: Duplicate key — another row also uses "{key}". Only one value per key can be saved.
envRowInvalid: Not a valid variable name — use letters, digits and underscores, and don't start with a digit.
envRowKeyRequired: Key required — a row without a key isn't saved.
envSaveFailed: Couldn't save the environment variables. Check the values and try again.
bulkParsedEmpty: Nothing to apply — paste KEY=value lines above.
dbLinksDesc: Attach a managed database — its connection URL is injected into this app's environment automatically on deploy.
dbLinksAdopt: Replace an app env var of the same name
dbLinksShadowed: overridden by an app env var
dbLinksNoDbs: No eligible database on this app's server. Create one on the same server to link it.
dbLinksRedeploy: Takes effect on the next deploy.
secretRefsDesc: Inject a value from a connected secret store into this app's environment on every deploy. Only the location is stored here, never the value.
secretRefsEnvVarInvalid: Use a POSIX name: a letter or _ then letters, digits or _.
secretRefsLocatorHint: Vault KV v2 path: <mount>/<path>#<field> — e.g. secret/myapp#DB_PASSWORD
secretRefsOverrides: replaces the app env var of the same name
secretRefsNoProviders: No secret store is connected for this team yet.
secretRefsProHint: External secrets are a Pro feature. Activate a license under Settings to bind one.
secretRefsRedeploy: Fetched fresh from the store on every deploy; a secret that can't be fetched fails the deploy.
buildArgsDesc: Injected at image build time (docker build --build-arg / buildpack --env). Visible in image history — don't store true secrets here. Applied on next deploy.
buildArgsRedeploy: Saved — redeploy to apply the new build arguments.
buildArgsSensitive: {keys} look like secrets. Build arguments end up in the image history — move them to Build secrets.
buildSecretsDesc: Mounted into the image build as BuildKit secrets — never written to a layer, docker history or a pushed image (the value is only ever on the build host, root-only, while the build runs). Dockerfile builds only; switching the build pack away from Dockerfile removes them. Applied on next deploy.
buildSecretsHow: Read a secret in your Dockerfile with RUN --mount=type=secret,id={key} … (file at /run/secrets/{key}); never COPY or ENV it.
buildSecretsRedeploy: Saved — redeploy to apply the new build secrets.
buildSecretsInvalidKey: Secret ids must be identifiers: letters, digits and _ ({keys})
buildSecretsNotDockerfile: Only a Dockerfile build can mount secrets. Switch the build pack to Dockerfile, or use build arguments for non-secret values.
buildSecretsLoadFailed: Could not load the build secrets — saving is disabled so nothing is overwritten.
sourceDesc: Change where this app's code or image comes from. Applied on the next deploy. Changing a repo to a different host resets the stored Git credential for safety.
sourceProviderNone: None (public repo or personal access token)
sourceProviderHint: Link a connected Git provider to clone a private repository without a personal access token. Only providers for this repository's host are listed.
sourceProviderTokenStored: A personal access token is stored for this app and is used for the clone.
sourceProviderSsh: This repository uses SSH, which clones with a deploy key — Git providers don't apply.
sourceProviderPrecedence: Takes precedence over a stored personal access token.
sourceProviderLinkedToast: Git provider linked — redeploy to apply.
sourceProviderUnlinkedToast: Git provider unlinked — redeploy to apply.
sourceWarn_git_token_cleared: The stored Git access token was cleared because the repository host changed.
sourceWarn_git_source_unlinked: The GitHub App was unlinked because the repository host changed.
sourceWarn_ssh_key_generated: A new SSH deploy key was generated — add its public key to the repository before deploying.
sourceWarn_git_commit_cleared: The pinned commit was cleared because the repository URL changed — deploys now track the branch HEAD.
buildSettingsDesc: Change how this Git app is built. Set a base directory to build a subfolder of a monorepo. Switching the pack clears the fields that don't apply to it. Applied on the next deploy.
buildDockerfilePath: Dockerfile path, relative to the base directory (Dockerfile)
buildSaveFailed: Could not update the build settings.
buildGitShallowHint: Fetch only the latest commit (faster). Always full history while a commit is pinned.
buildGitSubmodulesHint: Initialise and update submodules recursively after the clone. Private submodules on the same host use the repo's token; public submodules on any host work.
buildGitLfsHint: Requires an up-to-date agent image that includes git-lfs; the deploy fails clearly if it is missing. Off = pointer files only.
buildDisableCacheHint: Rebuild every layer on every deploy. Slower, but never reuses stale layers.
buildDisableCacheRailpack: Not available for the Railpack build pack (it has no cache-bypass option).
buildInjectEnv: Inject environment variables as build arguments
buildInjectEnvHint: Dockerfile builds only. Passes the app's environment variables to docker build as --build-arg, so the Dockerfile can read them with ARG. To choose individual variables instead, use Build time on each variable.
buildInjectEnvWarn: Build arguments are visible in the image history (docker history). Build-secret keys are excluded and the build log lists the variable names that were passed. Use build secrets for anything sensitive.
buildSourceCommitHint: Runtime sets SOURCE_COMMIT in the container (classic apps only).
buildSourceCommitBuildNote: Also passed to the build, so the Dockerfile needs ARG SOURCE_COMMIT. This invalidates the layer cache from that ARG onward on every new commit.
buildSourceCommitBuildEnvNote: Also exposed to the build as the SOURCE_COMMIT environment variable; this can invalidate the build cache on every new commit.
buildSourceCommitStaticNote: Static builds have no build arguments, so this is runtime-only for them.
dockerOptionsDesc: Advanced: raw flags appended to docker run (e.g. --cap-add, --sysctl, --dns, --add-host). Wrong flags can break the deploy. The traefik., tugra. and com.docker.compose|swarm|stack. label namespaces are protected. Applied on next deploy.
containerLabelsDesc: Applied on next deploy. Tugra ingress labels stay protected.
labelsAppliedHint: Derived on every deploy from this app's settings. They cannot be edited here.
labelsNoneApplied: Tugra applies no labels to this app right now.
labelsResetConfirmBody: All custom labels are removed on the next deploy. Labels Tugra applies itself are not affected.
labelsFromDockerOptionsHint: These come from --label flags in the Custom Docker options card. Edit them there.
labelsInvalidKey: "{key}" is not a valid label key.
labelsDuplicate: "{key}" appears more than once (keys are case-insensitive).
labelsTooMany: At most {max} custom labels are allowed.
labelsValueInvalid: The value of "{key}" is too long or contains control characters.
labelsComposeNote: Compose apps declare their labels in the compose file. Only the labels Tugra adds are listed above.
labelsSwarmNote: On a swarm these are container labels, applied through a rolling update on the next deploy.
labelsPreviewNote: Preview apps do not take custom labels.
labelsWhyTraefik: Tugra owns ingress routing on the shared proxy.
labelsWhyCompose: Docker Compose project and service identity.
labelsNoteRollingHealth: During a rolling deploy the new container also carries Traefik health-check labels until it takes over.
labelsNoteNeedsDomain: Routing labels appear once the app has a domain.
labelsNoteComposeUserLabels: Labels you write in the compose file are applied as they are and are not shown here.
labelsNoteImageLabels: Labels baked into the image itself are not shown.
labelsNoteSwarmContainer: Custom labels are set on the containers, not on the swarm service.
labelsNoteSwarmRuntime: Swarm adds a few runtime labels of its own at deploy time; they are not shown.
cloneWarn_custom_labels_dropped: Custom container labels were not copied because a compose app declares its labels in the compose file.
privilegedHint: Privileged host flags are allowed for this app — flags such as --privileged, --device, host namespaces and host bind-mounts can grant this container root on the host. Only enable for workloads you trust.
privilegedConfirmBody: This lets Docker options for this app escape container isolation and gain root-level access to the host (e.g. --privileged, --device, docker.sock, host mounts). Tugra ingress labels stay protected. Enable only if you own and trust this workload.
containerCommandDesc: Override the image's ENTRYPOINT and CMD. One argument per line, passed directly with no shell. For shell features set the entrypoint to sh and -c (one per line) and put the script in the command — the image must contain sh. Applied on the next deploy.
restartPolicyDesc: When Docker restarts this app's container. Defaults to "unless-stopped". An advanced Custom Docker options --restart still overrides this. Applied on the next deploy.
noContainers: No containers found (deploy the app first).
containerLogsDesc: Recent stdout/stderr from the running container (last 200 lines).
logsEmpty: No output (container not running or no logs yet).
liveLogsDesc: Live stdout/stderr streamed straight from the running container.
pickContainerToStream: Pick a container to stream its logs.
logsBeforeFirstDeploy: Container logs appear after the first deploy.
rollbackConfirm: Roll back to this deployment's image? The app will restart on the old version.
limitsDesc: Optional CPU, memory, swap, PID and shared-memory limits and the deploy timeout. Applied on next deploy.
limitsPrecedenceHint: A flag you also set in Docker options takes precedence.
memorySwapHint: Total memory plus swap. -1 = unlimited swap. Needs a memory limit.
pidsLimitHint: Caps the number of processes (PIDs). -1 = unlimited.
shmSizeHint: Size of /dev/shm. Docker's default is 64 MB.
cpuSharesHint: Relative share when CPUs are busy (2 to 262144, default 1024).
limitSwapNeedsMemory: Set a memory limit to use swap.
limitSwapBelowMemory: Memory + swap can't be below the memory limit.
limitCpusetInvalid: Use CPU numbers or ranges, like 0-3 or 0,2.
deploySettingsDesc: How a new version replaces the running one on each deploy.
rollbackOnFailure: Auto-rollback on a failed health check
rollbackOnFailureDesc: Off: a failed deploy stays down instead of restoring the previous version.
imagesToKeepDesc: How many past versions to keep for rollback (1–20; blank = 5). Lowering it prunes the extra images on the next deploy; the running version is always kept.
postCutoverSoakDesc: Zero-downtime rolling deploys only. After cutover Tugra keeps the previous version for this many seconds and reverts automatically if the new one fails 3 health checks in a row. New apps default to 30; 0 turns it off. Use at least 3x your health-check interval.
postCutoverSoakInactive: Not active: this app does not use a zero-downtime rolling deploy, so there is nothing to revert to.
postCutoverSoakProbes: About {count} health checks run during the soak window.
postCutoverSoakCannotTrip: {sec}s is under 3 health-check intervals, so it could never trigger a revert and the soak is skipped on deploy. Widen the window or shorten the health interval.
clusterDeployDesc: Deploy this app as a Docker Swarm service with N replicas spread across a cluster's swarm, instead of one server.
clusterDeployNote: Routed via the cluster's swarm Traefik (custom domain over TLS, or a wildcard DNS-01 magic domain when the manager node is configured with le-dns), or reachable on any node's host port when domainless. The manager node must be dedicated to the swarm (no classic apps on :80/:443). Logs are aggregated across replicas; the terminal opens a shell into one running replica (the node needs the 'terminal' capability); metrics show every task.
clusterNoSwarms: No cluster with a formed swarm in this team. Form a swarm on a cluster first.
clusterSaveFailed: Couldn't update the cluster deploy settings.
clusterCapacityWarn: {replicas} replicas across {online} online node(s) — some nodes will run more than one replica.
clusterPinnedBanner: Pinned to {node} because it has persistent storage.
clusterStatefulHint: This app has persistent storage (named volumes) — deploying it to a cluster hard-pins it to one node and locks replicas to 1.
clusterStatusUnavailable: Live replica status unavailable — the swarm manager may be offline.
clusterSaveToDeploy: Save to deploy to this cluster and see live replicas.
buildConfigDesc: Push the built image to a team registry on each deploy (portable images, multi-server, rollbacks).
buildServerHint: Build on a separate server, then pull the image to deploy (needs a registry).
buildNoRegistries: No registries in this team yet — add one under Container Registries.
healthCmd: Health check command (e.g. curl -fsS http://localhost:80/ || exit 1)
healthCheckDesc: How a new version is verified before it goes live. A failed check auto-rolls-back to the previous version. Applied on next deploy.
healthCheckResponseTextHint: Require this exact text in the response body, in addition to the status code.
placementDesc: Pin or spread this app's replicas across specific nodes. Every option is drawn from the cluster's live nodes.
placementNoLiveNodes: No live nodes to place onto yet — the cluster's manager may be offline.
placementNoLabels: No node labels yet — add some on the cluster page.
placementSaved: Saved — applied on the next deploy.
volumesDesc: Named volumes keep data across redeploys. Applied on next deploy.
hostMountsDesc: Mount a folder from the server into the app — e.g. your media library at /mnt/media for Jellyfin or Plex. Applied on next deploy.
hostMountsHint: System paths (/etc, /var, /home, /srv, the Docker socket, …) are blocked for safety. Read-only is recommended unless the app needs to write.
credentialsDesc: Access a private git repo or container registry. Stored encrypted; applied on next deploy.
gitTokenHint: For a private HTTPS repo on GitHub, GitLab, Gitea or a self-hosted server: paste a personal access token with read access to the repository.
deployKeyHint: Add this public key to the repository as a read-only deploy key (GitHub/GitLab/Gitea → Settings → Deploy keys), then deploy. The private key stays encrypted on the server.
deployKeyNone: This SSH repository needs a deploy key. Generate one, add the public key to the repo, then deploy.
deployKeyGenerated: Deploy key generated — add the public key to the repository
deployKeyRegenConfirm: Regenerate the deploy key? The current key stops working immediately: the next clone fails until you add the new public key to the repository.
deployKeyRemoveConfirm: Remove the deploy key? The app can no longer clone this repository until you generate and add a new one.
tasksDesc: Run a command inside the container on a cron schedule.
taskTimeoutHint: Seconds before the run is killed. Blank = the 300s default. Raise it for long jobs (backups, reports).
taskRunStarted: Task started — check its last run / notifications for the result.
previewDesc: Open a pull or merge request and Tugra deploys a throwaway copy on its own subdomain; close or merge it and it's torn down automatically.
previewEnable: Deploy a preview for each pull / merge request
previewNeedsDomain: Add a domain to this app first — previews are served at pr<n>.<domain>.
previewWildcardHint: Point a wildcard DNS record *.{domain} at this server so each preview URL resolves.
previewNone: No active previews. They appear here when a pull or merge request is opened.
previewForkNote: Requests from forks are never deployed; a preview builds a branch of this repository.
webhookHelpGithub: GitHub: content type application/json and the secret above; events Pushes and Pull requests.
webhookHelpGitlab: GitLab: the secret above as Secret token; triggers Push events and Merge request events.
webhookHelpGitea: Gitea / Forgejo: content type application/json and the secret above; events Push and Pull request.
webhookHelpBitbucket: Bitbucket Cloud / Server: set the webhook secret to the secret above; triggers Repository push and Pull request created, updated, merged, declined (Server: opened, source branch updated, merged, declined, deleted).
webhookDeliveryHint: If no preview appears, open the delivery in your git provider: the response says why the request was ignored.
exposeNoUrl: Saved, but no reachable URL could be built — this server has no public IP or wildcard domain (or it's a Compose app). Set a host port or a wildcard domain.
exposeApplyNote: Applied to the proxy on the next deploy.
tunnelExposedOn: App is now reachable through the Cloudflare Tunnel
tunnelExposedOff: App removed from the Cloudflare Tunnel
tunnelExposeDesc: Route this app's domain through the server's tunnel so it's reachable from the internet with no public IP.
tunnelExposeNeedsDomain: Give the app a domain first (magic or custom), then it can be routed through the tunnel.
exposeModeDesc_magic: Auto domain from the server's IP — reachable instantly, no DNS setup.
exposeModeDesc_custom: Your own domain, served over HTTPS (Let's Encrypt).
serviceDomainsDesc: Route individual compose services to their own hostnames (each over HTTPS). Give the service name, a hostname pointed at this server, and the service's container port. Up to 20. Applied on the next deploy.
serviceDomainsRedeploy: Saved — redeploy to apply the service domains.
serviceDomainsSaveFailed: Could not update the service domains.
extraDomainsDesc: Additional hostnames served by this app alongside the primary domain, each over HTTPS. Point each at this server, then redeploy. Up to 10.
extraDomainsRedeploy: Saved — redeploy to apply the new domains.
extraDomainsSaveFailed: Could not update the extra domains.
dnsAutoDesc: Point this domain at your server with a Cloudflare API token — apex A (+ www) records, created for you. DNS-only, so there's no proxy redirect loop.
dnsAutoWildcardLink: Need a wildcard (*.example.com) certificate, or one while the record stays Cloudflare-proxied? Set up DNS-01 on this server →
dnsAutoApiTokenHint: Create a token with Zone:DNS Edit and Zone:Zone Read for this domain's zone.
dnsAutoApplied: DNS records created — it can take a few minutes to propagate.
dnsAutoConflictNote: Some records already exist and point elsewhere. Enable overwrite to replace them.
dnsAutoManualToggle: Not using Cloudflare? Set up manually
dnsAutoManualDesc: Create these records at your DNS provider, then save the domain.
domainRedeployNote: Point this hostname at your server, then redeploy to apply.
domainOptionsDesc: Redirect and security headers for this domain. Applied on next deploy.
gzipDesc: Compress responses at the proxy (Traefik compress middleware). Already-compressed or tiny responses are skipped.
forwardAuthDesc: Protect this app behind an external auth service (Authelia, oauth2-proxy, Authentik). Every request is verified there first. Leave empty to disable.
customCertDesc: Serve your own TLS certificate for this app's domain instead of Let's Encrypt — paste the certificate chain (PEM) and its private key. The key is encrypted at rest and never shown again. Applied on the next deploy.
certClearConfirm: Remove this custom certificate? Redeploy the app afterwards to finish the switch — until you do, HTTPS serves a temporary self-signed certificate. It then falls back to Let's Encrypt.
certUploaded: Certificate stored — redeploy the app to start serving it.
certCleared: Custom certificate removed — redeploy the app to finish switching off it.
depNotFound: This deployment does not exist or belongs to another app.
depForbidden: You need write access to this app to view its deployment logs.
depConfigNoBase: No earlier configuration to compare with.
depConfigUnchanged: Configuration unchanged since the previous deployment.
depNote_interrupted: The hub restarted while this deploy was in progress and its result could not be recovered. The app's status was left untouched — re-deploy to be sure.
depNote_recovering: The hub lost its connection to the agent during this deploy. The deploy keeps running on the server and is picked back up automatically when the agent reconnects.
depNote_auto_rollback: The new version failed its health check, so the previous version was kept (or restored). The app is still serving the old version.
depNote_cancelled: This deploy was cancelled before it finished. Check the app's status for the version currently serving.
depLiveFollowing: Live — following the build on the agent
depLiveTruncated: The live buffer keeps the last 64 KiB; the full log is saved when the deploy finishes.
depLiveUnavailable: No live log is available for this run (the hub restarted or is recovering the deploy from the agent). The full log appears when it finishes.
gpusNotChecked: GPU detection hasn't run on this server yet.
gpusNone: No GPU detected on this server.
gpusAdvice_noGpu: No GPU was detected on this server, so this container may fail to start.
gpusAdvice_nonNvidia: This server only has non-NVIDIA GPUs, and Docker's --gpus flag is NVIDIA-only.
gpusAdvice_noDriver: An NVIDIA GPU was found but its driver isn't loaded, so GPU containers can't use it yet.
gpusAdvice_runtimeUnconfirmed: The NVIDIA runtime isn't confirmed on this server. GPU containers may still work if the NVIDIA Container Toolkit is installed.
gpusAdvice_countExceeds: You asked for more GPUs than this server has ({n} detected).
gpusAdvice_indexOutOfRange: A device index here isn't among this server's {n} detected GPU(s).
gpusAdvice_deviceUnknown: That GPU UUID isn't among this server's detected GPUs.
cloneWarn_gpus_unavailable_on_target: This app requests GPUs but the target server has no detected NVIDIA GPU. The setting was kept; check it before deploying.
iuStateNoBaseline: Redeploy once so Tugra can record this image's digest
iuStatePinned: Pinned to a digest — nothing to update
iuStateUnsupported: This image reference can't be checked for updates
iuErr_unsupported: this server's agent can't run checks — update the agent
iuErr_failed: the registry could not be reached from the agent
iuHint_unsupported: Update the agent on this server from the Servers page, then check again.
iuHint_failed: The check runs from the agent container, so a registry that is reachable only through the Docker daemon (custom CA, insecure registry, mirror or proxy) cannot be probed.
iuToggleHint: Probes the registry from this app's server about every 6 hours.
envFlagBuildHint: Passed to the image build. On Dockerfile and static builds it is baked into the image history (docker history) - use Build secrets for secrets.
envFlagRuntimeHint: Turn off to make this a build-only variable that never reaches the running container.
envFlagLiteralHint: Compose stacks: the value is never expanded ($VAR and ${VAR} stay as written).
envFlagLiteralInert: This app type already passes every value literally.
envFlagMultilineHint: Allow line breaks (PEM keys, JSON). Delivered to the container by name through the Docker CLI's environment: never written to the env file and never a docker argument. The name must use letters, digits and underscores, and cannot be one that changes how Docker itself runs (for example PATH, HOME, DOCKER_*, LD_*, *_PROXY).
envFlagsUnavailable: Variable flags could not be loaded, so this editor shows every variable as a plain one. You can still edit and save values; the stored flags are kept.
envFlagsCorrupt: The stored flags for this app's variables are unreadable. Until they are reset, deploys fail closed. Reset clears every flag (build time, literal, multiline); set the ones you need again afterwards.
envFlagsResetBody: This saves the variables shown here and clears every stored flag (build time, build-only, literal and multiline). Set the ones you need again afterwards.
bulkUnterminated: A quote is never closed on {keys}, so the rest of the text would be read as one value. Close the quote or remove it.
envMultilineAutoOn: Turned on Multiline for {count} variable(s) that contain line breaks.
envRowNewline: This value has line breaks. Turn on Multiline to keep them.
envRowMultilineKey: A multiline variable name must use letters, digits and underscores and cannot be a reserved name.
envRowLiteralKey: A literal variable name must use letters, digits and underscores and cannot be a reserved name.
envRowBuildKey: A build-time variable name must use letters, digits and underscores.
envRowBuildSource: Build-time variables apply to Git-built apps only.
envRowRuntimeOffNeedsBuild: A variable that is off at runtime must be available at build time.
envRowTooLarge: A multiline value can be at most {max}.
envBuildSensitiveWarn: This name looks like a secret. Build-time values are visible in the image history.
envSaveFailedDetail: Could not save the environment variables: {detail}
buildConfigImageNameHint: Repository path pushed to, appended to the registry namespace (lower-case letters, digits, . _ - and up to 3 "/" separators). Leave empty for tugra_<app id>. Each name can belong to one app per registry.
buildConfigAliasTagHint: An extra tag pushed next to the immutable one, e.g. latest or {branch}. It moves on every build (last built, not last deployed) and a rollback does not move it. A registry with immutable tags rejects it and fails the deploy; leave it empty then.
buildConfigPreviewAlias: Alias tag, moves on every build, not on rollback
buildConfigNeedsPush: Pick a registry and enable push to set an image name or alias tag.
buildConfigRepoTaken: Another app already pushes to that repository in this registry.
buildConfigNameInvalid: Not a valid image name. Use lower-case path components (letters, digits, . _ -), at most 4, no tugra_ prefix.
buildConfigAliasInvalid: Not a valid alias tag. Use letters, digits, . _ - and {sha} / {branch}; it must not look like a deployment id.
buildInlineDockerfileHint: Used with docker build -f. The repository is still the build context, so COPY paths resolve against it. Put secrets in Build secrets, not here.
buildInlineOverrides: The inline Dockerfile is used instead of this path.
buildInlineTooLarge: The Dockerfile is larger than 48 KiB.
buildInlineInvalid: The Dockerfile must start with FROM (only ARG may come before it) and contain no NUL byte.
deployHooksComposeDesc: Run a command in one service of this compose stack. The pre-deploy command runs in a one-off container of that service before the stack is brought up; a failure aborts the deploy with the current stack still serving. The post-deploy command runs inside the service once it is up and never fails the deploy. Single-server apps only; applies on the next deploy.
deployHooksServiceHint: The compose service both commands run in.
deployHooksServiceRequired: Pick the service the hook runs in.
deployHooksDetectFailed: Could not read the services from the compose file.
deployHooksPreComposeHint: Runs before the stack is brought up. The service's image is pulled or built first, and its dependencies are started so a migration can reach its database, including on the first deploy. If the command fails those dependencies keep running; the service itself is never recreated.
deployHooksPostComposeHint: Runs after the stack is up, once the service is running (and healthy when it has a health check). A failure is logged and ignored.
composePreviewNote: Variables are shown unresolved, literal environment and build-arg values are redacted, and the routing override Tugra adds on deploy is not included.
composePreviewUnsupported: The agent's Docker Compose is too old for this preview. Update Docker Compose on the agent.
composePreviewBusy: A preview is already running for this app. Try again in a moment.
composePreviewFailed: The compose could not be previewed.
composePreviewOffline: The agent is offline, so the compose cannot be rendered right now.
moveDesc: Relocate this app, with its data, to another server of the same team. It keeps its identity (same app ID, settings, secrets, webhooks and history). This is a cold move: the app is stopped on the current server, its volumes are copied, and it is started on the new one.
moveLockedTooltip: This app is being moved to another server — this action is paused until the move finishes.
moveClusteredDisabled: Swarm/cluster apps can't be moved with this tool.
moveNoTargets: There is no other server in this team to move the app to.
moveVolState_absent_skip: nothing to copy (not on the server)
moveNoVolumes: This app has no data volumes: only its configuration moves.
moveDowntimeNone: No downtime: this app was never deployed, only its configuration moves.
moveLinkResult: Link between the servers: about {mbps} Mbit/s
moveColdMoveNotice: This is a COLD move. The app is stopped on the current server and is unavailable until it is healthy on the new one. Its data is copied, never deleted: the current server keeps a stopped copy until the archive period ends.
moveAckHostMounts: I understand that data in host bind mounts is NOT copied.
moveAckExternalVolumes: I understand that external / named compose volumes are NOT copied (they start empty on the new server).
moveAckDropPrivileged: I allow dropping the privileged Docker options grant on the new server (owner only).
moveAckDropGpus: I allow dropping the GPU request (the new server is not ready for it).
moveAckResetCpuset: I allow resetting the CPU pinning (the new server has fewer cores).
moveAckHostPortChanged: I accept that the host port changes to a free one on the new server.
moveAckDomainChanges: I understand the app's domain(s) change or must be pointed at the new server.
moveRepointDns: Repoint the DNS records Tugra manages for this app's domains
moveRetainDays: Keep the old copy of the data for
moveConfirmLabel: Type the app name to confirm
moveStartFailed: The move could not be started.
moveCancelConfirm: Cancel the move? The app will be started again on the current server.
moveCompleted: The app now runs on the new server.
moveCompletedBody: The old server keeps a stopped copy of the data until {date}.
moveCompletedNoArchive: The old server's copy of the data was removed.
movePurgeConfirm: Remove the old copy of this app's data from the previous server now? This cannot be undone.
moveRolledBackBody: Your app is running on the original server. Reason: {reason}
moveFailedNeedsAttention: The move failed and needs your attention.
moveFailedBody: The app could not be brought back up on the original server ({reason}). Its data on that server was not touched. Fix the server, start the app by hand, then clear this alert.
moveFailedClearConfirm: Clear this alert? Tugra removes what the failed move left on the new server only when the app is back on the original server. If the app runs on the new server, nothing there is removed. A kept recovery copy of replaced data, if there is one, is removed too.
moveSnapshotKeptNote: A copy of data the transfer replaced is kept on the new server because the transfer could not be undone cleanly. It is not removed automatically.
moveSnapshotPurgeConfirm: Remove the kept copy of the replaced data from the new server now? This cannot be undone.
rollbackPredatesMove: This deployment ran on the app's previous server and only exists there as a local image — it can't be rolled back to.
moveBlocker_same_server: Pick a different server than the one the app already runs on.
moveBlocker_cross_team: The target server belongs to another team.
moveBlocker_app_is_preview: A preview app can't be moved; it follows its parent app.
moveBlocker_agent_offline_source: The app's current server is offline. Bring it back online first.
moveBlocker_agent_offline_target: The target server is offline. Pick another one or bring it back online.
moveBlocker_probe_failed: A preflight check on a server failed or gave unusable output. Try again; if it keeps failing, check that server's agent.
moveBlocker_agent_too_old: A server's agent is too old to move apps. Update it first (Servers, Update agent). An agent that cannot update itself cleanly has to be moved by hand once.
moveBlocker_capability_missing: A server has not been granted the deploy and backup capabilities a move needs.
moveBlocker_no_curl: curl is not installed on a server; the data transfer needs it.
moveBlocker_no_tool: A tool the transfer needs (split, sha256sum or gzip) is missing on a server.
moveBlocker_cluster_app: Swarm/cluster apps can't be moved with this tool.
moveBlocker_target_in_cluster: The target server is a node of a cluster's swarm.
moveBlocker_previews_exist: Delete the app's preview deployments first.
moveBlocker_db_links_exist: Unlink the app's managed databases first; their network routes are per-server.
moveBlocker_db_network: Turn off the database network first; it is local to one node.
moveBlocker_rollout_active: A fleet rollout is working on this app. Wait for it to finish.
moveBlocker_deploy_active: A deployment is queued or running. Wait for it to finish.
moveBlocker_move_active: This app already has a move in progress.
moveBlocker_move_active_on_server: Another app move is using the current or the target server. One move per server at a time.
moveBlocker_move_needs_attention: The last move of this app failed and needs attention. Clear it (Remove old copy) after fixing the server.
moveBlocker_migration_import_active: A migration import is still filling this app. Wait for it to finish (or cancel it) before moving the app.
moveBlocker_alias_conflict: The app's container alias is already used by another app on the target server.
moveBlocker_network_alias_conflict: A network alias or network name of this app collides with another app on the target server.
moveBlocker_ports_conflict: Ports this app publishes are already in use on the target server. Change the app's extra or compose ports first.
moveBlocker_target_volume_exists: A Docker volume with the same name already exists on the target server and is not an archive of an earlier move of this app.
moveBlocker_bad_volume_name: A volume name is not safe to hand to Docker. Rename the volume first.
moveBlocker_disk_insufficient: There is not enough free disk space on a server for the transfer.
moveBlocker_build_server_offline: The app's build server is offline.
moveBlocker_link_probe_failed: The link test between the servers failed. The hub's address may not be reachable from an agent, or a proxy in front of the hub limits request sizes (lower MOVE_PART_MIB).
moveBlocker_privileged_not_owner: Only the instance owner can move an app that holds the privileged Docker options grant.
moveBlocker_external_volume: Compose external or named volumes are not copied; the new server starts them empty.
moveBlocker_host_mounts: Data in host bind mounts is not copied.
moveBlocker_privileged_options: The privileged Docker options grant (and the stored options) is dropped on the new server.
moveBlocker_gpus_unavailable: The new server is not ready for the app's GPU request; the request is dropped.
moveBlocker_cpuset_exceeds: The app's CPU pinning names a core the new server doesn't have; it is reset.
moveBlocker_host_port_changed: The app's host port is busy on the new server; a free one is used instead.
moveBlocker_domain_changes: The app's generated domain changes with the server address, or your custom domain must be pointed at the new server.
moveWarn_dns_manual_repoint: Your custom domain's DNS must point at the new server ({ip}). Tugra can do this for domains it manages if you tick the option.
moveWarn_magic_domain_changes: The generated domain changes because it embeds the server address.
moveWarn_self_urls_rewritten: The app's own address inside its compose file and config files is rewritten for the new server.
moveWarn_env_may_reference_old_host: Some environment variables mention the old server ({keys}); they are NOT rewritten.
moveWarn_env_may_reference_old_host_noke: Some environment variables mention the old server; they are NOT rewritten.
moveWarn_local_backups_stranded: {count} local volume backup(s) stay on the old server and can't be restored from the new one (S3 backups are fine).
moveWarn_history_splits: Metrics and traffic history split at the move: older data stays under the old server.
moveWarn_image_may_differ: The image tag is pulled again on the new server; a mutable tag (like latest) may resolve to a newer image.
moveWarn_git_rebuild: The app is rebuilt from Git on the new server; the result may differ from the running build.
moveWarn_tunnel_resync: The Cloudflare tunnel ingress is re-synced for the new server.
moveWarn_xattrs_acl_not_preserved: File ACLs, extended attributes, symlink ownership and directory timestamps are not preserved by the copy (file contents, modes, owners and timestamps are).
moveWarn_custom_cert_redelivered: The app's uploaded TLS certificate is delivered to the new server again.
moveWarn_archive_overwritten: A stopped copy of this app's data from an earlier move on the target is overwritten by this move.
moveWarn_source_volume_absent: A declared volume has no data on the current server: nothing to copy, it is created on first start.
moveWarn_stopped_app_started_briefly: The app is stopped: it is started briefly on the new server to prove it runs there, then stopped again.
moveWarn_tls_http01_gap: A Let's Encrypt certificate for your custom domain can't be issued until the domain's DNS points at the new server.
moveWarn_proxy_will_be_installed: The new server has no Tugra proxy yet; it is installed on the first deploy.
moveWarn_deploy_failed_after_move: The app failed to start on the new server. It was already failing before the move, so it stays there.
moveWarn_dns_repoint_failed: Some DNS records could not be repointed: {hostnames}. Do it by hand.
moveWarn_source_cleanup_failed: The old container could not be removed from a server; remove it by hand.
moveWarn_staging_cleanup_failed: Temporary files could not be removed from a server; they are harmless and can be deleted by hand.
moveWarn_post_cutover_sync_failed: Some follow-up syncs failed ({steps}); they retry on the next change.
moveWarn_target_stop_failed: The app could not be stopped again on the new server after the test start.
moveWarn_apply_snapshot_kept: A copy of the data the transfer replaced was kept on the new server as {snapshot} because the transfer could not be undone cleanly. It is not removed automatically; use Remove old copy now once you are sure you do not need it.
moveErr_preflight_changed: The situation changed after the move was planned. Run the checks again.
moveErr_agent_offline: A server's agent went offline during the move.
moveErr_stop_failed: The app could not be stopped on the current server.
moveErr_stop_unverified: The app was still running on the current server after it was stopped.
moveErr_prepare_failed: The new server could not be prepared.
moveErr_pack_failed: The data could not be packed on the current server.
moveErr_part_stat_failed: A part of the data could not be measured.
moveErr_transfer_failed: A part of the data could not be transferred.
moveErr_size_mismatch: A transferred part arrived with the wrong size.
moveErr_sha_mismatch: A transferred part failed its checksum.
moveErr_apply_aborted: The data could not be unpacked on the new server; nothing was changed there.
moveErr_apply_rolled_back: Unpacking the data failed and was rolled back on the new server.
moveErr_apply_rollback_failed: Unpacking the data failed and its rollback failed on the new server.
moveErr_apply_failed: Unpacking the data failed on the new server.
moveErr_entry_count_mismatch: The unpacked data did not match the original.
moveErr_changed_under_us: The app was changed by someone else during the move.
moveErr_cutover_failed: Switching the app to the new server failed.
moveErr_deploy_failed: The app failed to start on the new server.
moveErr_deploy_timeout: The app did not become healthy on the new server in time.
moveErr_hub_restarted: The hub restarted during the move.
moveErr_deadline_exceeded: The move took too long and a server stayed offline.
moveErr_source_restart_failed: The app could not be restarted on the original server.

domainDnsChallenge.label: Issue the certificate with DNS-01
domainDnsChallenge.desc: Issues this domain's certificate through a DNS challenge instead of HTTP-01, so it can be ready before the domain points at this server. Applied on the next deploy.
domainDnsChallenge.enabledToast: DNS-01 enabled — applies on the next deploy
domainDnsChallenge.disabledToast: DNS-01 disabled — applies on the next deploy
domainDnsChallenge.noCreds: This server has no DNS-01 credentials. Set them up in the server's network settings first.
